sentences.text: An environment variable is like the table number in each restaurant of a chain.
The menu is the same, but the local detail changes.
This way the same agent works in Dev, Test, and Production without editing it.
Think of one menu that is identical everywhere, with one small value that changes in each place.
The types are Decimal number, Text, J S O N, Two options, Data source, and Secret.
The base U R L of an A P I is a good example of the Text type.
For example, the base address of an A P I can be Text, but a password should be Secret, never Text.
The Secret type stores a reference to a secret in Azure Key Vault.
The real secret does not live in Dataverse or in the solution, and only Azure Key Vault is supported.
You have to register the resource provider in the subscription, and give the Key Vault Secrets User role to the person who creates the variable.
Before you export, you can remove the current value, so you do not carry the development value.
When you import, you are asked for the value of the new environment.
This way each environment uses its own values, and nobody carries the development setup into production by mistake.
In Copilot Studio, the variables are read-only.
The published agent includes the values from when it was published, so you republish after a change, except with Secret, which is retrieved at runtime.
It is an easy detail to forget, so memorize it before the exam.
